title: The Devotee To Whom Allah Gave a Cloud

keywords: the devotee to whom allah gave a cloud
full_text:
An ascetic hermit who had spent thirty years living in a mountain cave, fasting and praying, noticed a wondrous sign: whenever he walked across the scorching desert trails, a small, white cloud hovered directly above his head, shielding him from the blazing heat of the sun. The hermit felt a secret pride, thinking: 'Surely, my thirty years of solitary fasting have made me the most beloved servant in the realm.'

One morning, the hermit noticed that the cloud was drifting away from him, moving across the valley and hovering over the head of a sun-darkened young peasant who was plowing a rocky hillside with a pair of oxen.

Perplexed and humbled, the hermit followed the cloud to the field and asked the peasant: 'Brother, what great spiritual austerities do you practice, that the cloud of mercy leaves my head to shade yours?'

The young farmer wiped his brow and smiled: 'I know nothing of austerities, venerable father. I plow this hard field from dawn until dusk. When the harvest comes, I divide my grain into three portions: one portion I give to the poor of our village, the second I sell to buy seeds and bread, and the third portion I carry to my ancient, bedridden parents, whom I bathe, feed with my own hands, and comfort with cheerful songs every evening.'

The hermit fell to his knees in the furrow, weeping in profound realization. He saw that thirty years of solitary prayers in a cave could not equal a single day of loving, dutiful service to elderly parents and honest toil for the hungry.

He returned to the city, sought out the sick and the aged, and spent the remainder of his life serving his fellow human beings, having learned that true holiness dwells in active love.
moral: Caring for aging parents and honest labor in the fields carry more spiritual merit than solitary contemplation.
